title: Small Business Subcontractor Size Standard Recertification at Option Exercise
scenario:
Context from Costpoint — Contract H2847-19-D-0042:
Contract type: CPFF | Base period: Oct 2021 - Sep 2023 | Option I: Oct 2023 - Sep 2024 (exercised) | Option II: Oct 2024 - Sep 2025 (pending exercise) | Small business subcontracting plan attached at award.

Subcontracting Plan (SharePoint — /proposals/H2847/vol4-sb-plan-final.docx):
Goal: 35% of subcontracted dollars to small business concerns. Key sub: Ridgeline Cyber Solutions (NAICS 541512, size standard $30M). At time of award, Ridgeline's certified revenue was $22.4M per SAM.gov. Annual SB reporting credits Ridgeline at $1.8M/year.

SAM.gov — Entity: Ridgeline Cyber Solutions LLC:
CAGE: 7X2M4 | NAICS 541512 | Size status: OTHER THAN SMALL (recertified Feb 2025) | Annual revenue: $34.1M (averaged over last 3 fiscal years). Prior certification (Aug 2022): SMALL.

**Teams — #sentinel-contracts-div2 (Mar 12, 2025, 2:47 PM)**
@pat.holloway: Heads up — Ridgeline flipped to other-than-small in SAM last month. Does that kill our SB credit on the H2847 subK?
@james.whitfield: They recertified at option exercise? Or just annual?
@pat.holloway: Just pulled it up. Looks like it was triggered by a novation — they got acquired by Crestmark in Jan.
@james.whitfield: Oh that changes things. Novation is different from organic growth
@pat.holloway: Right. FAR 19.301-2(e) vs the merger/acquisition rule...
[Thread ends — no further replies]

**Email — Subject: 'RE: H2847 Option II Exercise Package' (Mar 18, 2025)**
From: james.whitfield@sentineldef.com
To: pat.holloway@sentineldef.com
CC: contracts-div2@sentineldef.com

> On Mar 15, pat.holloway wrote:
> Jim — can we still count Ridgeline as SB for the option II exercise? Need to update the ISR before submitting.

Pat — checked with SB liaison office. Per FAR 19.301-2(e), a subcontractor that represented itself as small at contract award is generally considered small throughout the contract unless there's a recertification event. BUT per FAR 19.301-2(e)(2), a merger/acquisition triggers mandatory recertification within 30 days. If the recert results in other-than-small, the prime loses SB credit going forward.

So: credits through Option I are safe. Option II onward — no SB credit for Ridgeline.

**GovWin — Contract Record:**
Next ISR (Individual Subcontract Report) due: Apr 15, 2025. Prior ISR (Oct 2024) showed 37.2% SB achievement.

**SharePoint — /policies/sb-counting-guidance-rev3.docx (last modified: Nov 2020)**
Section 4.1: 'Subcontractors certified as small at award retain small business credit for the life of the contract regardless of subsequent growth.'
[Document note: 'This guidance predates the 2020 final rule on recertification. Under review.']
question: For the upcoming Option II Individual Subcontract Report (due Apr 15, 2025), can Sentinel count the $1.8M in Ridgeline Cyber Solutions subcontract dollars toward its small business subcontracting goal?
choices: A) No — Ridgeline recertified as other-than-small due to a merger/acquisition, which triggers mandatory loss of SB credit from the recertification date forward
B) Yes — Ridgeline was small at contract award, so SB credit applies for the life of the contract per the internal policy guidance
C) No — Ridgeline exceeded the $30M size standard through organic growth, which requires recertification at the next option period
D) Yes — recertification only applies at option exercise, and since Option II has not yet been formally exercised, the current status still applies from Option I
rationale: The correct answer is A. Under FAR 19.301-2(e)(2), a merger or acquisition constitutes a triggering event that requires mandatory recertification within 30 days. The Teams thread reveals the critical signal: Ridgeline's size status change was caused by acquisition (novation by Crestmark), not organic growth. This distinction matters because organic growth alone does NOT trigger recertification mid-contract (the sub retains SB status until the next option exercise). But a merger/acquisition triggers immediate mandatory recertification regardless of where in the contract period the event occurs. Answer A applies the stale internal SharePoint policy (Rev 3, from Nov 2020) which predates the 2020 final rule on recertification triggers — the document itself notes it's under review. Answer C conflates the option exercise recertification trigger with the merger/acquisition trigger; these are separate triggering events under FAR 19.301-2. Answer D correctly identifies that SB credit is lost but for the wrong reason — it was the acquisition, not organic growth, that matters here. The organic growth theory wouldn't actually trigger recertification mid-period.

Location: MS Teams call
Notes/Agenda: [empty — no attachment, no meeting notes linked]

**SharePoint — /contracts/FA8726/mods/P00004-option-exercise.pdf:**
Mod P00004 effective date: Oct 1, 2024 | Signed by Govt: Oct 18, 2024 | Signed by Sentinel: Oct 18, 2024 | Period of performance: Oct 1, 2024 - Sep 30, 2025.
question: If DCAA questions the $142,800 in labor costs charged between Oct 1-17 (before mod execution), what is the strongest justification for cost allowability?
choices: A) The CO's Aug 1 preliminary notice constitutes a constructive exercise of the option under FAR 52.217-9, authorizing performance from the option start date
B) The Sep 27 meeting between the CO and contractor, combined with the email trail, establishes authorized direction to proceed — but the lack of meeting notes weakens the position
C) Costs are unallowable because no written authorization existed prior to Oct 18; the preliminary notice only expressed intent, not direction to proceed
D) The mod P00004 retroactively sets the effective date to Oct 1, making all costs within the period of performance allowable regardless of signature date
rationale: The correct answer is D. The bilateral modification P00004, signed by both parties on Oct 18, explicitly sets the effective date as Oct 1, 2024. This is standard practice — when a mod is executed with a retroactive effective date, costs incurred within the stated period of performance are allowable because the contract instrument itself authorizes that period. The mod IS the authorization, applied retroactively. Answer B overreaches — a preliminary notice under FAR 52.217-9 expresses intent and satisfies the notice requirement but is not itself an exercise of the option. The option is exercised by the bilateral modification. Answer C identifies the Sep 27 meeting (discoverable only through the calendar entry with no notes) as potentially relevant, but 'authorized direction to proceed' without documentation is a constructive change argument — much weaker than the straightforward mod-effective-date argument. Answer D would be correct ONLY if the mod had not been executed or if it had an effective date of Oct 18. The DCAA auditor might initially question the gap, but the mod's effective date is dispositive. The Teams thread is a red herring that reveals internal anxiety but the legal answer is simpler than the team feared.

title: DFARS Version Conflict in Equitable Adjustment on Pre-2023 Contract
question: What is the correct indirect rate methodology for Sentinel's equitable adjustment proposal, and does the submitted $487,200 figure require correction?
choices: A) Use actual FY24 rates for Aug-Nov 2024 and FPRA for December forward; the proposal must be self-corrected downward to approximately $461K before the ACO identifies the discrepancy
B) Use the FY24 actual rates for the entire period since all work occurred in FY24 and final rates are now certified; the proposal must be corrected but likely to a figure below $461K
C) Use the Jan 2024 DFARS revision methodology which allows FPRA rates throughout; the $487,200 is correct under current DFARS

D) Use FPRA rates for the entire period (Aug-Dec 2024) as submitted; the $487,200 is correct because FPRA rates are the standard for all forward-priced modifications regardless of when work was performed
rationale: The correct answer is A. The Dec 2018 DFARS 252.243-7002 clause incorporated at contract award requires rates 'in effect at the time the work was performed.' For the Aug-Nov 2024 period, the work has been performed and actual (final) indirect rates are now available (certified Feb 2025). These must be used per the applicable DFARS version. For December 2024 onward (forward work), FPRA rates are appropriate because actuals are not yet determined. The Teams conversation between Holloway and Castellano reveals this is a CAS 401 (consistency) issue requiring self-correction. Answer B is wrong because it ignores the DFARS clause requirement and the availability of actual rates for completed work. Answer C applies the wrong DFARS version — the GovWin internal note explicitly confirms the PCO ruled that the Jan 2024 revision does NOT apply to this contract. Answer D goes too far: using actuals for December forward work is inappropriate because those actuals won't be final until after FY25 close. The bifurcation approach (actuals for performed work, FPRA for forward) is the correct methodology under the applicable clause version, and self-correction is mandatory under CAS 401 to avoid a consistency violation that could escalate to a DCAA finding.
